query1: 1. Which idea is more novel? (“More novel” means the idea is creative, distinct from existing work, and brings fresh insights. Consider whether similar ideas have already appeared in papers — including preprints — and feel free to search online before judging.)
query2: 2. Which idea is more feasible to implement as a short research project? (Assume a typical CS PhD student has 1–2 months, access to OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, but limited GPU compute. “More feasible” means it’s more practical to execute given these constraints — with fewer flaws, lower resource needs, and less complexity.)
query3: 3. Which idea is more likely to work well in practice (i.e., outperform existing baselines)? (“More likely to work” means the idea has fewer flaws, and you expect it to yield better results than current methods on relevant benchmarks — either in general or in key scenarios.)
query4: 4. Which idea is more exciting and potentially impactful if fully executed as a research project? (“More exciting” means it could make a meaningful contribution to the field — from being accepted at a major AI conference to possibly transforming the field or winning awards.)
query5: 5. Which idea is stronger overall and more likely to be accepted at a top AI conference (e.g., ACL, ICLR, NeurIPS)? (“Stronger overall” means the idea is better in terms of clarity, novelty, feasibility, effectiveness, and impact — the kind of project you’d score higher using the 1–10 scale for major AI conferences.)
query6: 6. Which idea is better grounded in existing scientific literature? (“Better grounded” means more of the key ideas, terms, or methods are clearly supported by relevant citations, prior work, or established concepts — not speculative or hallucinated.)
query7: 7. Which idea is more clearly motivated by prior research? (“More clearly motivated” means the idea addresses a known gap, trend, or limitation in existing literature with a compelling and well-grounded rationale.)
query8: 8. Which idea has a more coherent and logically integrated composition? (“More coherent” means the methods, variables, and tasks fit together naturally, with clear rationale and support from existing literature.)
query9: 9. Which idea presents a clearer and more testable research goal or direction? (This includes either an explicit hypothesis or a well-defined research objective. “Clearer” means it’s easier to understand what the project aims to test or achieve, and how success could be evaluated.)
